summary: Partial source-audited link mapping for regular quadratic forms over arbitrary number fields: 35 incoming core-supplier links, two outgoing Hasse–Minkowski integration links, and one keep-boundaries overlap. Exact two-sided excerpts preserve canonical completions, local/archimedean hypotheses, discriminant conventions, norm-index and reciprocity distinctions. One pre-existing Spin normal-form edge is not duplicated. Six precise gaps/clarifications and catalogue-screening limits are recorded; no implementation or independent-review claim is made.

gaps.title: Incorrect discriminant-sign explanation in the source README
gaps.detail: GlobalQuadraticForms 5.1 says (-1)^(n(n-1)/2)=-1 in dimension four. In fact (-1)^6=+1, so the signed and plain discriminants agree in dimension four. Retain the declared plain-discriminant convention, but correct that explanatory sentence through a separately authorised source edit. This job does not modify content/.

gaps.title: Stale supplier layer number for weak approximation
gaps.detail: GlobalQuadraticForms names GlobalNumberFields Layer 0.2 in its contract discussion. In the pinned supplier README and extract the named weakApproximation_denseRange theorem is in Layer 1: weak approximation and multiplicative congruences. The link uses that actual stage ID. Correct the textual locator without changing the mathematical requirement from density to a congruence-only corollary.

gaps.title: A principal-idele bridge does not supply the required arbitrary-idele theorem
gaps.detail: The pinned CFT Layer 13 explicitly constructs principalIdele_mem_range_ideleNormMap_iff for x in K units. GQF 4.2 and 4.4 require mem_range_ideleNormMap_iff for an arbitrary i in I_K. The stronger named statement was not found in the checked supplier README/search. Required statement: for a finite separable extension E/K, an arbitrary idele i lies in the range of the canonical idele norm exactly when every finite and infinite coordinate is a norm from the corresponding finite étale completion algebra. Prove the converse using unit norm-surjectivity outside the finite ramified/nonunit set and restricted-product assembly; derive the existing principal case. The theorem itself need not assume cyclicity; cyclicity belongs to the global-element Hasse norm theorem. The maps must be the supplied canonical maps, with explicit comparison to ideleFiniteCoord and ideleInfiniteCoord.

gaps.title: The Hilbert character of an arbitrary idele needs its own finite-support bridge
gaps.detail: GQF 4.4 step 2 defines φ(i)=product_v (i_v,b_v). The preceding product theorem is stated for two global units. For an arbitrary idele i, establish support containment using the finite nonunit support of i, the support of the fixed global b, the dyadic places and archimedean places. Then use the odd-residue unit-unit symbol formula. This adaptation is not an application of global reciprocity to a nonexistent global representative of i.

gaps.title: Explicit nonzero choice in the empty-exceptional-set branch
gaps.detail: In GQF 5.4 the local neighborhoods force Q(x) nonzero only when T is nonempty. If T is empty, choose a global vector of the regular binary U with Q(x) nonzero (or add one auxiliary place/neighborhood) before defining b. The theorem is not contradicted; this is a small but explicit missing branch in the displayed proof route.
